description:
First three photos are all of an infrutescence that had fallen and caught in a vine below the tree. 
The next two photos show the canopy from different angles. Then there is a zoom shot into the canopy, I'm trying to show you the several infrutescences in the tree, but the wind is blowing. With my binoculars I can see that while the infrutescence hangs down, the fruits point back upward. Most of the fruits are still green. 
Then two shots of the trunk, it's a twin trunk tree, about 5" dbh. The twig was the only one I could reach, it is dead wood. No leaves are in reach but see linked observations for leaves from younger plants nearby. 
I think this is probably a wild tree, it is not in a yard but in an adjacent forest conservation area with no indications of intentional planting.

This is the first sapling found, maybe 50ft NE of the fruiting tree. All of the little saplings were right on the tree line inside the fence that forms the boundary between the forest conservation area and the subdivision lawn.
There were maybe four more plants, all within a few feet of each other. If these trees have runners, then these could all be one individual. If not, the are probably separate saplings.
Apparently wild
